summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and coronary artery disease, was admitted with acute chest and epigastric pain, following an episode of syncope. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome due to normal troponins and EKG. Elevated lipase and clinical presentation confirmed acute pancreatitis, likely alcohol-induced, with gallstones considered less likely given imaging findings. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and analgesia, then advanced to a low-fat diet. His pain stabilized, and he tolerated oral intake. A transient cough resolved with PRN albuterol. Hypertension was managed with an increase in lisinopril from 20 mg to 40 mg daily. He remained stable, with no signs of alcohol withdrawal. He was discharged home with instructions to maintain a low-fat diet, abstain from alcohol, continue home medications, and follow up with primary care and hepatology.
